questions: How many devices did you fabricate and cool down, and how many showed the excess noise? Your Methods (p. 8) and Supplementary Note 1 (p. 16) answer part of this: three devices measured, four datasets, all with the same behavior.
Were any devices, cooldowns or QPC settings set aside, and why?
Which ranges did you measure beyond the ones shown: QPC reflection settings, magnetic field across the ν = 5/2 plateau (the field value isn't given), temperature, and bias beyond |e*VS/2kBT| ≈ 6?

What does the second-best dataset look like? Figs. S1 to S3 show it; why do your Fig. 2b (data set 4) and Fig. 3b (data set 3) come from different datasets, when the outlook rests on their "simultaneous agreement" (p. 7)?

How did you determine the 10 mK electron temperature, how far do the PH-Pf and A-Pf predictions in Figs. 2b and 3b move for an error of a few mK, and what uncertainty sits behind "within experimental uncertainty" (p. 7)?
Can you extract the scaling dimension from the bias dependence of RQPC (nearly flat in Figs. S1 to S4, panels a and e) and recompute the Fano factors with it?
Did you run either two-QPC configuration on an integer channel of these devices, to size any braiding-like signal from interaction between co-propagating channels?

The main text says the heating noise is "far smaller than the measured noise" (p. 7) and Fig. S9 says the model "underestimates the measured excess noise by roughly a factor of two" (p. 39); how do these fit together, and is there a heating estimate for the charged configuration?
